# Evaluating the Contour Integral

## Setting Up the Problem

I need to evaluate $\oint_{|z|=10} \frac{e^z}{4z^2 + 9\pi^2}\, dz$.

**Factoring the denominator:**

$$4z^2 + 9\pi^2 = 4\left(z^2 + \frac{9\pi^2}{4}\right) = 4\left(z - \frac{3\pi i}{2}\right)\left(z + \frac{3\pi i}{2}\right)$$

So the integrand has simple poles at $z_1 = \frac{3\pi i}{2}$ and $z_2 = -\frac{3\pi i}{2}$.

## Checking Which Poles Are Inside the Contour

$$|z_1| = \frac{3\pi}{2} \approx 4.71 < 10 \quad \checkmark$$
$$|z_2| = \frac{3\pi}{2} \approx 4.71 < 10 \quad \checkmark$$

Both poles lie **inside** the circle $|z| = 10$.

## Computing the Residues

**Residue at $z_1 = \frac{3\pi i}{2}$:**

$$\text{Res}(z_1) = \frac{e^{z_1}}{4(z_1 + 3\pi i/2)} = \frac{e^{3\pi i/2}}{4 \cdot 3\pi i} = \frac{e^{3\pi i/2}}{12\pi i}$$

Since $e^{3\pi i/2} = \cos\frac{3\pi}{2} + i\sin\frac{3\pi}{2} = -i$:

$$\text{Res}(z_1) = \frac{-i}{12\pi i} = -\frac{1}{12\pi}$$

**Residue at $z_2 = -\frac{3\pi i}{2}$:**

$$\text{Res}(z_2) = \frac{e^{z_2}}{4(z_2 - 3\pi i/2)} = \frac{e^{-3\pi i/2}}{4 \cdot (-3\pi i)} = \frac{e^{-3\pi i/2}}{-12\pi i}$$

Since $e^{-3\pi i/2} = \cos\frac{3\pi}{2} - i\sin\frac{3\pi}{2} = i$:

$$\text{Res}(z_2) = \frac{i}{-12\pi i} = -\frac{1}{12\pi}$$

## Applying the Residue Theorem

$$\oint_{|z|=10} \frac{e^z}{4z^2+9\pi^2}\,dz = 2\pi i\left[\text{Res}(z_1) + \text{Res}(z_2)\right] = 2\pi i\left(-\frac{1}{12\pi} - \frac{1}{12\pi}\right)$$

$$= 2\pi i \cdot \left(-\frac{1}{6\pi}\right) = -\frac{2\pi i}{6\pi} = -\frac{i}{3}$$

## Result

$$\boxed{-\dfrac{i}{3}}$$
